text: Clara Burel, born on 24 March 2001, is a French professional tennis player who peaked at No. 42 in the WTA singles rankings on 10 June 2024. In 2018, she reached the junior singles final at the Australian Open, the US Open, and the Youth Summer Olympics (YOG), and won a mixed-doubles bronze medal with compatriot Hugo Gaston at the YOG. She qualified for the ITF Junior Masters in October 2018, winning her first major title and becoming the junior world No. 1 the following week on 29 October 2018. Burel was selected as an alternate in the French Fed Cup team for the 2018 first-round match against Belgium. In September, she reached her first final on the ITF Circuit in Clermont-Ferrand, losing to Lesley Kerkhove. She was a wildcard entrant at the Australian Open, where she lost in the first round to Carla Suárez Navarro. In March, she received a wildcard into the Lyon Open but lost in the first round to Jil Teichmann. In September at Strasbourg, she defeated Kateryna Bondarenko before losing to Zhang Shuai in the second round. At the French Open, she entered as a wildcard, defeated Arantxa Rus in the first round and Kaja Juvan to reach the third round—becoming the youngest Frenchwoman since 18-year-old Alizé Cornet achieved the same in 2008—before losing to Zhang Shuai for the second consecutive tournament. She qualified for the Australian Open again, losing to Alison Van Uytvanck in the first round. Burel made her top 200 debut on 8 March 2021, rising 37 positions to world No. 181 after reaching the quarterfinals in Lyon. She qualified for Wimbledon, making her first main draw appearance at the grass-court Grand Slam, defeating Ellen Perez before losing in the second round to Kaja Juvan. Burel reached her first WTA Tour final at the Ladies Open Lausanne, losing to Tamara Zidanšek, and achieved her top 100 debut at world No. 98 on 19 July 2021. She made her WTA 1000 debut at the Canadian Open as a qualifier, losing to 13th seed Ons Jabeur in the first round. Burel reached a new career-high WTA singles ranking of No. 74 on 21 February 2022 and recorded her first WTA 1000 win at the Miami Open against qualifier Magdalena Fręch, though she lost to 28th seed Petra Kvitová in the second round. She qualified for the US Open, reaching the third round by defeating 25th seed Elena Rybakina and Alison Van Uytvanck, before losing to sixth seed Aryna Sabalenka. Burel qualified for the Australian Open again, defeating wildcard Talia Gibson in the first round, her first win at this major. In April, she qualified for the WTA 1000 Madrid Open, losing to Camila Osorio in the first round and then to 20th seed Barbora Krejčíková in the second round. She reached the final at the Ladies Open Lausanne, losing to Elisabetta Cocciaretto. Burel won her first WTA 125 title at the Open Angers Arena Loire in December, defeating compatriot Chloé Paquet in three sets. At the Australian Open, she reached the third round for the first time at this major, defeating Aleksandra Krunić and fifth seed Jessica Pegula, her first top-10 win, before losing to Océane Dodin, which led to a new career-high singles ranking of world No. 44, reaching the top 50 for the first time on 5 February 2024. At the Upper Austria Ladies Linz, she reached the quarterfinals, defeating Sinja Kraus and Kateřina Siniaková, before losing to third seed Donna Vekić. At the upgraded WTA 500 in Strasbourg, she reached the quarterfinals, defeating wildcard Karolina Plíšková and seventh seed and defending champion Elina Svitolina, her second career top-20 win, before losing to third seed Danielle Collins. Burel recorded a first-round win over Eva Lys at Wimbledon, losing her next match to qualifier Sonay Kartal. At the Cleveland Open, she reached the quarterfinals, defeating lucky loser Elvina Kalieva and eighth seed Sofia Kenin, before losing to top seed Beatriz Haddad Maia. Moving to the US Open, she defeated former champion Sloane Stephens but lost to 20th seed Victoria Azarenka in the second round. On her debut at the China Open, she won her first-round match over lucky loser Tamara Korpatsch before losing to fourth seed Coco Gauff in the second round. Only main-draw results in WTA Tour, Grand Slam tournaments, Billie Jean King Cup, United Cup, Hopman Cup, and Olympic Games are included in win–loss records. The information is current through the 2024 Jasmin Open and the 2024 US Open.
